_doc: CLOCKWORK-1: every loop is a clock with an expected interval and a source of beats; `python3 -m foundation clock --report` measures them (ticking, late, stopped, idle) and the result is published on /live. A stopped or inaccurate clock is a defect. `chain` is how the executor keeps ticking between its daily cron: a run that ends with takeable work wakes the next run, capped per day and backed off after failures; the Actions budget guard still applies.

clocks.what: the org's heartbeat on Cloudflare (cron every 10 minutes): reconcile, claims, gates, predictions, dispatch

replicas.why: ultrastable account, primary since the 2026-11-15 cutover (ACCOUNT-SPLIT-2)

clocks.what: the unattended executor: takes the top backlog item through the code agents to a pull request
the public live record on ultrastable.io/live
merge to live site deploy
the weekly scout of the state of the art: sources read, findings filed, sources re-weighted
A11Y-LOOP-1: the weekly accessibility and layout audit of every public page
CRITICALITY-LOOP-1: one beat per tick from the tick Worker's criticality controller (act on k_eff, grade the last action)

replicas.why: ultrastable account, primary since the 2026-11-15 cutover (ACCOUNT-SPLIT-2)

clocks.what: words checked against code and the deployed site
RESILIENCE-1: the GitHub watchdog that probes every clock and restarts the stopped ones; the tick Worker dispatches it again when it is older than 12 hours
the daily trend read: series per component, loop and entry, and what they show

Unlearn tenant beat (cron 41 * * * * on ultrastable-unlearn; a visit catches up a silent cron): check a batch of encyclopedia entries against Crossref and Europe PMC, re-learn coaching move weights, measure, open the next phase, prune
the daily intent yield: every owner directive's own probe, restatements charged to the original, /yield

What Works tenant beat (cron 17 * * * * on ultrastable-what-works; a visit catches up a silent cron): check a batch of programmes against Crossref, OpenAlex and Europe PMC (a refusing index rested for an hour, one beat at a time), read new trials in, re-grade and log every move

Replication Ledger tenant beat (cron 23 * * * * on ultrastable-replication-ledger; a visit sparks one when the last is over two hours old): search OpenAlex for new replications and new landmark findings, file attempts under a verbatim-quote guard, check Crossref, recompute standings and log every move
the weekly re-verification of funding registry rows at their primary sources
the daily cost reading against budgets (D1 rows read, Workers AI neurons) and the criticality log
the weekly export and restore drill of every D1 database and KV namespace
the daily publish of gate-cleared posts and the thought-leadership pass
the weekly rebuild of the demo video from the storyboard (pushes to the storyboard also start it; only scheduled and dispatched runs are beats)
the weekly outreach pass: programmes, packets, guard, queue and the intro lane
the daily spinoff pass over the idea queue and the free-tier headroom
the daily product manager pass: growth mix, insight findings, improvement items
the daily fleet queue pass across every repository: dispositions, balance, drift (the tick Worker may also dispatch it; every run is a beat)
the daily issue sweep: triage and SLA (issue events also start the workflow; only scheduled and dispatched runs are beats)
the weekly re-triage of open issues
UIUX-1: the weekly browser audit of every user page and path
the daily clean-room bootstrap: a sandbox system from the seed alone, a simulated day, teardown, and the satellite agent-file coherence check

stages.what: an executor run started (it reaches the model route)
an unattended pull request was opened
an unattended pull request merged to main
the site deployed after the last change to it (merge to live lag)

escalation.what: wake the stage's own workflow now (bounded per day)
change the approach: run the next takeable item instead of the one that is stuck
file a repair item for the product manager (p0) and show it on the public record

settlement.close_comment: Settled as expired by CLOCKWORK-1: no merge within the settlement window; the item returns to the queue under its own name.

_doc_replicas: A d1 clock reads every replica (one per Cloudflare account; ACCOUNT-SPLIT-2 runs the tick on whichever is primary) and the newest beat from any of them counts. Found 2026-11-17 by RESILIENCE-1: the clock read only the standby database and reported a 45 h stall while the primary ticked every 10 minutes.
_doc_health: A d1 clock may also name public /health URLs (one per account); the started_at of last_tick from any of them is a beat. This needs no credential, so a host without access to the primary account's database still sees the primary tick (RESILIENCE-1, 2026-11-17: the GitHub token read only the standby database).
